title: Tenant scenario blueprints, defaults serializer and quant bundles
author: Celeste Rivera
release_notes: Adds tenant scenario blueprints (declarative defaults for batching/caching), a serializer CLI to export/import tenant default bundles, and packaged quantization profiles. Exposes tenant-level unit-econ estimates in telemetry. Backwards-compatible; opt-in via tenant defaults file.
description:
Motivation: Many tenants hit similar cost/latency tradeoffs but require different conservative defaults. This PR introduces a compact, versioned "blueprint" format for tenant scenarios (workload shape, latency SLO, budget tier) and a serializer CLI to persist and import per-tenant default bundles. It also bundles curated quantization profiles that map to these blueprints so we can recommend deterministic defaults for batching, cache windowing, and quantization in a single artifact.

What this PR does (high level):
- Introduces a tenant scenario blueprint schema (pkg/econ/blueprint.go) that captures workload percentiles, preferred latency svc, and budget constraints.
- Implements a serializer/deserializer CLI (cmd/blueprintctl) to export tenant defaults as a single .rwbundle (yaml+metadata) so operators and SEs can review and apply them.
- Packages three conservative quantization bundles (safe-int8, balanced-q4, latency-q3) and adds a registration hook so runtime can pick a compatible profile automatically when a blueprint is applied.
- Adds heuristics to derive batching and KV-cache defaults from blueprint fields: target-batch-ms, max-prefill, and cache-ttl suggestions.
- Emits per-tenant unit-econ estimates and a small set of telemetry labels (econ.blueprint.id, econ.estimated-per-token, econ.batch-suggested) for downstream dashboards and alerts.

Design notes:
- Blueprints are intentionally opinionated and conservative by default; they are meant to accelerate safe rollouts rather than be the only control plane.
- The serializer produces a signed metadata bundle (HMAC) to ensure we can validate imported presets on Private installs.
- Quant bundles are small JSON manifests that describe quantization type, model-compatibility hints, and expected quality delta ranges. Runtime has a compatibility translator to fall back safely when the exact quantization isn't available.

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests for blueprint parsing and serialization (tests/econ/blueprint_serializer_test.go).
- Integration smoke tests that apply a blueprint to a small dedicated pool and assert the runtime picks a compatible quant bundle and sets batching/cache knobs.
- Local perf-suite run on benchmark-lab with 3 workload shapes to assert cost delta estimates are within 8% of observed cost on avg.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge to main behind feature-flag "blueprint-import".
2) Run canary in benchmark-lab and on a small set of opt-in tenants (eng-internal).
3) After 2 weeks of stability and telemetry verification, flip default opt-in for newly created tenants and provide UI/CLI hooks for existing ones.
4) Ship docs and CLI examples (docs/telemetry/tenant_blueprints.md).

Migration and backward compatibility: The change is opt-in. Existing tenant configs remain unchanged. The serializer is additive and imports will only apply when a tenant admin explicitly applies the bundle.

Files changed (high-level): pkg/econ/blueprint.go, pkg/econ/serializer.go, cmd/blueprintctl/main.go, configs/defaults/tenant-frugal.yaml (new bundles), runtime/quant/registry.go (small compatibility adapter), observability/metrics/econ_metrics.go, docs/telemetry/tenant_blueprints.md, tests/econ/blueprint_serializer_test.go, examples/blueprints/sample-rwbundle.yaml, sdk/python/redwood/econ_defaults.py

Known limitations:
- The unit-econ estimator uses a simplified cost model (per-chip token costs + KV cache hit heuristics) and must be validated for extreme workloads; warnings are emitted in telemetry for out-of-distribution shapes.
- Quant bundle compatibility is best-effort; we refuse to apply a bundle that is incompatible with the pinned model family.

Related work: ENG-1482 (tenant defaults effort), ENG-2339 (unit-econ telemetry).

review_comments:
Marcus Lee (review): Nice end-to-end. A few safety asks: ensure import does not overwrite live tenant overrides and add an audit event.

Author reply: Added import-guard and an audit event in observability/metrics/econ_metrics.go - see latest commit.

Ivy Chen (review): Can we make target-batch-ms a soft suggestion in the runtime so downstream autoscalers can override?

Author reply: Implemented as suggestion metadata; runtime will respect only if tenant policy is 'default'. Added doc note.
Ravi Kapoor (approval): Verified on benchmark-lab against 3 profiles. Telemetry labels look good. Approving to merge.
rollout_plan: feature-flagged merge, canary on benchmark-lab and opt-in tenants for 2 weeks, flip opt-in for new tenants and document CLI import/export
notes_for_ops: To validate after rollout: check econ.estimated-per-token vs cost.seen token metric and ensure no unexpected spike in cache hit metrics. If issues, disable blueprint-import flag and revert via standard rollback.
changelog_excerpt: Add blueprint serializer and tenant default bundles; bundle safe quantization profiles and emit unit-econ telemetry. Opt-in; no breaking changes.
